text:
Anna L: Quick RFC follow-up — we prototyped moving penalty/score calc out of the policy compiler and into the runtime sidecar. Seeing some surprising perf and operator tradeoffs, want to align on next steps.
Chris D: summary please — what surprised you?
Anna L: TL;DR: runtime calc simplified compile-time policy bundles, reduced hot-reload complexity, but introduced CPU jitter on p95 in small payloads. Also made deterministic simulation harder.
Mike S: CPU jitter meaning bursts during high QPS? numbers?
Anna L: yes, bursts. On dev cluster, p95 token-latency for short responses increased ~12% under sustained 10k rps with penalties enabled. p50 unchanged.
Jess H: interesting — could be due to penalty evaluation not being vectorized or cache-unfriendly lookups. Did we include telemetry for cache hits?
Anna L: added counter metrics: penalty-eval-duration, cache-hit, cache-miss. Miss rate was ~37% for tenant affinity lookups on small seqs.
Chris D: what are core tradeoffs we care about? my list: 1) determinism for sims/evals 2) runtime perf headroom 3) deployment surface (hot reload complexity) 4) observability granularty 5) ability to experiment with heuristics quickly
Mike S: add 6) failure isolation: runtime failures shouldn't take whole serving process down.
Jess H: If we keep calc in compiler, we bake results (or approximations) into routing table which is great for sims and stable latency. Con: policy changes need recompile and rollout — slower experiments.
Anna L: Right. Moving to runtime gives faster experiment velocity and per-request signals (region, transient load) but costs CPU and more complex telemetry to prove parity.
Chris D: Could we do hybrid? precompute coarse-grained penalties at compile-time (per-model/per-region) and do small delta adjustments at runtime for transient signals.
Mike S: hybrid seems promising. Precomputed table reduces lookups, runtime applies a cheap delta: e.g. final_penalty = base_penalty + clamp(runtime_delta, -X, +Y). Keep runtime_delta inexpensive.
Jess H: Agree. We should define a runtime micro-contract: delta eval must be O(1) and have a 95th percentile budget like <= 50us. If it exceeds, fallback to base_penalty.
Chris D: Also need API surface for the compiler->runtime proto. Minimal fields: route_id, base_penalty, model_tags, region_hint, last_updated_ts. Keep it small.
Anna L: Proposed migration plan: 1) Instrument current runtime penalty eval with more fine-grained histograms and tracepoints (2 weeks) 2) Implement base_penalty export from compiler into route metadata (1 week) 3) Deploy hybrid delta evaluator behind feature flag (canary) (2 weeks) 4) Run sim/eval to compare routing decisions end-to-end (1 week)
Mike S: fallback behavior: if delta eval slow or panics, we must increment a circuit-breaker metric and serve base_penalty. No retries.
Jess H: test plan: create unit sims that pin latency/penalty differences with synthetic region load traces. Also add e2e smoke to ensure no decision divergence > 0.5% on control workloads.
Chris D: ops checklist: add alert if penalty-eval-duration.p95 > 50us OR if cache-miss-rate > 10% after rollout.
Anna L: decision points for next week: A) Accept hybrid approach B) pick clamp limits for delta (+/- 0.2 by default) C) land minimal proto for route metadata
Jess H: I vote A+B+C. Start with conservative clamp and tune.
Mike S: +1. I'll draft the proto and the fallback circuit breaker bits.
Chris D: I'll take on the sim harness updates and the alerting rules.
infra-bot: deploy-check: canary pipeline created for feature flag "hybrid-penalty-delta". See <https://ci/internal/pipe/2398>.
Anna L: thanks — I'll post the RFC follow-up doc in the architecture docs folder after we sync on clamps and timelines.
Chris D: great sync. we should also note long-term: if delta logic grows beyond O(1) we should push it back into compile-time or a dedicated scoring service. Keep the runtime contract strict.
Anna L: agreed — long-term we may extract a scoring microservice if heuristics become ML-based. For now hybrid + strict budget.
Jess H: sounds good. end of thread.
